How to perform MMT • Patients are asked to hold a position against a therapist’s resistance. • It is important to stabilize proximal part of the area being tested to reduce compensatory action by muscles other than those being tested • Resistance needs to be applied gradually ("meet my resistance" or "don't let me move you") in the opposite direction of muscle being tested • Both sides should be tested to provide a comparison

How to perform MMT
• Patients are asked to hold a position against a therapist’s resistance.
• It is important to stabilize proximal part of the area being tested to reduce compensatory action by muscles other than those being tested
• Resistance needs to be applied gradually ("meet my resistance" or "don't let me move you") in the opposite direction of muscle being tested
• Both sides should be tested to provide a comparison

Manual Muscle Testing (MMT)
• Assessment of muscle strength
• Manual muscle testing is a procedure for the evaluation of the function and strength of individual muscles and muscle groups based on the effective performance of a movement in relation to the forces of gravity and manual resistance.
• Dynamometry is a method of strength testing using sophisticated strength measuring devices (e.g., hand-grip, hand- held, fixed, and isokinetic dynamometry).

Muscle Strength Grading Scale (Oxford Scale)
No contraction
Visible/palpable muscle contraction but no movement
Movement with gravity eliminated
Movement against gravity only
Movement against gravity with some resistance
Movement against gravity with full resistance

How to perform MMT
• Patients are asked to hold a position against a therapist’s resistance.
• It is important to stabilize proximal part of the area being tested to reduce compensatory action by muscles other than those being tested
• Resistance needs to be applied gradually ("meet my resistance" or "don't let me move you") in the opposite direction of muscle being tested
• Both sides should be tested to provide a comparison

Testing Position
• Anti-Gravity
• Gravity Eliminated (for weaker muscle)
• Supine
• Side-lying
• Prone
• Sitting
